source.title: Commentary Critical and Explanatory on the Whole Bible
source.author: Robert Jamieson, A. R. Fausset and David Brown
source.edition: CCEL expanded electronic edition of the 1871 public-domain text

entries.heading: 2. put a knife
entries.text: 2. put a knife --an Eastern figure for putting restraint on the appetite.

entries.heading: 3. are deceitful meat
entries.text: 3. are deceitful meat --though well tasted, injurious.
4, 5. (Compare 1Ti 6:9, 10 ). thine own wisdom --which regards riches intrinsically as a blessing.

entries.heading: 5. Wilt . . . eyes
entries.text: 5. Wilt . . . eyes --As the eyes fly after or seek riches, they are not, that is, either become transitory or unsatisfying; fully expressed by their flying away.
6-8. Beware of deceitful men, whose courtesies even you will repent of having accepted. evil eye --or purpose ( Pr 22:9; De 15:9; Mt 6:23 ).

entries.heading: 8. The morsel . . . words
entries.text: 8. The morsel . . . words --that is, disgusted with his true character, all pleasant intercourse will be destroyed.
9. (Compare Pr 9:8 ). "Cast not your pearls before swine" ( Mt 7:6 ).

entries.heading: 11. redeemer
entries.text: 11. redeemer --or avenger ( Le 25:25, 26; Nu 35:12 ), hence advocate ( Job 19:25 ). plead . . . thee --(Compare Job 31:21; Ps 35:1; 68:5 ).
12. Here begins another series of precepts.
13, 14. While there is little danger that the use of the "divine ordinance of the rod" will produce bodily harm, there is great hope of spiritual good.
15, 16. The pleasure afforded the teacher by the pupil's progress is a motive to diligence.

entries.heading: 16. my reins
entries.text: 16. my reins --(Compare Ps 7:9 ).
17, 18. (Compare Margin ). The prosperity of the wicked is short.

entries.heading: 18. an end
entries.text: 18. an end --or, "hereafter," another time, when apparent inequalities shall be adjusted (compare Ps 37:28-38 ).

entries.heading: 19-21. guide . . . way
entries.text: 19-21. guide . . . way --or direct thy thoughts to a right course of conduct (compare Pr 4:4; 9:6 ).

entries.heading: 20. riotous . . . flesh
entries.text: 20. riotous . . . flesh --prodigal, or eating more than necessary. Instead of "their flesh" (compare Margin ), better, "flesh to them," that is, used for pleasure.

entries.heading: 21. drowsiness
entries.text: 21. drowsiness --the dreamy sleep of the slothful.

entries.heading: 22. Hearken
entries.text: 22. Hearken --that is, obey ( Pr 1:8; Eph 6:1 ). despise . . . old --Adults revere the parents whom, as children, they once obeyed.

entries.heading: 23. Buy
entries.text: 23. Buy --literally, "get" ( Pr 4:5 ). truth --generally and specially as opposed to errors of all kinds.

26-35. A solemn warning against whoredom and drunkenness ( Ho 4:11 ). give me --This is the address of that divine wisdom so often presented ( Pr 8:1; 9:3 , &c.). heart --confidence. observe --keep. my ways --such as I teach you ( Pr 3:17; 9:6 ).

entries.heading: 27, 28. deep ditch
entries.text: 27, 28. deep ditch --a narrow pit, out of which it is hard to climb. lieth in wait --to ensnare men into the pit, as hunters entrap game (compare Pr 22:14 ).

entries.heading: 28. increaseth . . . transgressors
entries.text: 28. increaseth . . . transgressors -- ( Pr 5:8-10 ). The vice alluded to is peculiarly hardening to the heart.
29, 30. This picture is often sadly realized now. mixed wine --(Compare Pr 9:2; Isa 5:11 ).

entries.heading: 31. when . . . red
entries.text: 31. when . . . red --the color denoting greater strength (compare Ge 49:11; De 32:14 ). giveth . . . cup --literally, "gives its eye," that is, sparkles. moveth . . . aright --Perhaps its foaming is meant.
32. The acute miseries resulting from drunkenness contrasted with the temptations.
33, 34. The moral effects: it inflames passion ( Ge 19:31, 35 ), lays open the heart, produces insensibility to the greatest dangers, and debars from reformation, under the severest sufferings.

entries.heading: 35. awake
entries.text: 35. awake --that is, from drunkenness ( Ge 9:24 ). This is the language rather of acts than of the tongue.
